description: Core principles of classical and modern physics

newtons_laws.first_law: An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and direction, unless acted upon by an unbalanced force (Law of Inertia).
newtons_laws.second_law: Force equals mass times acceleration: F = ma. The acceleration of an object depends on its mass and the net force applied.
newtons_laws.third_law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

energy_forms.potential: Stored energy due to position: PE = mgh (gravitational)
energy_forms.electromagnetic: Energy carried by photons and EM waves
energy_forms.nuclear: Energy stored in atomic nuclei, released via fission or fusion

thermodynamics_laws.zeroth: If two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third, they are in equilibrium with each other.
thermodynamics_laws.first: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed (conservation of energy).
thermodynamics_laws.second: Entropy of an isolated system always increases; heat flows from hot to cold spontaneously.
thermodynamics_laws.third: As temperature approaches absolute zero, entropy approaches a minimum value.

electromagnetic_spectrum.microwaves: 1 mm – 1 m; used in radar and cooking
electromagnetic_spectrum.visible_light: 380–700 nm; detectable by the human eye

waves.doppler_effect: Change in frequency/wavelength of a wave in relation to an observer moving relative to the wave source.
waves.interference: Superposition of waves; constructive when peaks align, destructive when peaks meet troughs.

relativity.special_relativity: Laws of physics are the same for all non-accelerating observers; speed of light is constant regardless of observer motion.
relativity.mass_energy_equivalence: E = mc²; mass and energy are interchangeable.
relativity.time_dilation: Moving clocks run slower relative to stationary ones.
relativity.length_contraction: Objects moving at relativistic speeds appear shorter in the direction of motion.
